posts.heading: November 12, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 21 species on November 12, with 18 heard, 10 seen, and 7 both, across 53 feeder visits. That is well below the past week's average of 91.0 visits, while the 238 detections ran above the 221.1 average, and the species count of 21 sat close to the 21.6 average.

Northern Cardinal, Eastern Towhee, Carolina Wren, Tufted Titmice, American Crow, Blue Jays, Carolina Chickadees, Northern Mockingbird, Song Sparrow, and White-throated Sparrow were all recorded on each of the past seven days, including this one. Eastern Phoebe and Mourning Dove, both recorded on earlier days this week, were not recorded today. No species was seen or heard at this station for the first time today.

The audio source was switched many times during the day, moving between the pi, c120, and pi-mic (movo-dom1) inputs, and each detection comes from whichever source was active at the time. The higher detection total should therefore be read with that mixed setup in mind rather than as more birds present.

posts.heading: November 11, 2026
posts.text:
The day was quieter than the past week, with 34 feeder visits against a seven-day average of 126.0 and 160 detections heard against 216.9. Twenty species were recorded, close to the average of 22.1. Northern Cardinal led with 38 detections heard and 3 seen, and Red-shouldered Hawk (24 heard) and Eastern Towhee (20 heard) were also prominent.

Eleven species recorded on every one of the past seven days, including this one, held again: American Crow, Blue Jay, Carolina Chickadee, Carolina Wren, Eastern Phoebe, Eastern Towhee, Northern Cardinal, Northern Mockingbird, Song Sparrow, Tufted Titmouse, and White-throated Sparrow. Ruby-crowned Kinglet returned after its last record on 2026-11-04, seen once as a probable. White-breasted Nuthatch, recorded on six of the previous seven days, was not recorded today, and no species was new to the station.

The audio source was switched repeatedly between the pi, pi-mic (movo-dom1), and c120 sources from 04:35 to 07:30, so the heard counts draw on mixed sources. The first visual record was a Northern Cardinal 4 min before sunrise, and the last was a Blue Jay 452 min after sunrise, 172 min before sunset.

posts.heading: November 10, 2026
posts.text:
November 10 added up to a quieter day at the feeders than the week before it: 19 species, 34 feeder visits, and 213 detections heard, against weekly averages of 21.4 species, 127.9 visits, and 218.0 heard. The 34 visits were the fewest of the eight days in the record, while the heard total sat close to its average. The first visual was a Tufted Titmouse 31 min after sunrise, and the last was a Northern Cardinal 8 min after sunset.

Eleven species were recorded on all seven days in the past week, including today, among them Northern Cardinal, Tufted Titmice, White-throated Sparrow, Carolina Chickadees, and Eastern Towhee. Northern Cardinal led the visual count with 8 confident visits, and Tufted Titmouse had 5. The Hermit Thrush returned after 11 days away, with a single detection, and Mourning Dove was seen twice, having been recorded on five of the seven days. House Finch and Red-bellied Woodpecker, recorded on five and four of the prior days respectively, were not recorded today.

There was no first confident visual at this station and no species heard for the first time. The audio source was switched many times during the day, so detections came from more than one microphone. The previous day, November 9, had 16 species and 62 visits.

posts.heading: November 9, 2026
posts.text:
November 9 added up to 62 feeder visits and 164 heard detections across 16 species, quieter than the past week's averages of 129.7 visits, 236.0 heard detections and 21.6 species. Eastern Towhee led the heard count with 33 and Northern Cardinal led the visits with 7, while Carolina Chickadee had the first visual of the day 23 min before sunrise and White-breasted Nuthatch the last, 315 min after sunrise. No species had its first confident visual record at this station on this day.

Eleven species were recorded on all seven days of the past week, including this one: American Crow, Blue Jay, Carolina Chickadee, Carolina Wren, Eastern Phoebe, Eastern Towhee, Northern Cardinal, Song Sparrow, Tufted Titmouse, White-breasted Nuthatch and White-throated Sparrow. House Finch, recorded on six of the previous seven days, was not recorded today.

American Robin was heard for the first time at this station, with 10 detections, after being away for 15 days since October 25. The audio source was switched many times through the day, beginning at 06:20, among the pi, c120 and pi-mic (movo-dom1) sources.
